simple.meaning: עִוָּרוֹן (ʻivvârôwn) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “blindness.” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 3 times across Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Zechariah, beginning at Leviticus 22:22. Its contexts include offering, altar.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עִוָּרוֹן (H5788).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: עִוָּרוֹן (ʻivvârôwn) / H5788 is traced through Leviticus 22:22, Deuteronomy 28:28, Zechariah 12:4 as a generated source-based concept entry.

firstOccurrence.englishText: You shall not offer what is blind, is injured, is maimed, has a wart, is festering, or has a running sore to Yahweh, nor make an offering by fire of them on the altar to Yahweh.

timeline.evidenceText: You shall not offer what is blind, is injured, is maimed, has a wart, is festering, or has a running sore to Yahweh, nor make an offering by fire of them on the altar to Yahweh.
Yahweh will strike you with madness, with blindness, and with astonishment of heart.

In that day,” says Yahweh, “I will strike every horse with terror, and his rider with madness; and I will open my eyes on the house of Judah, and will strike every horse of the peoples with blindness.

definitions.full: H5788. ivvarown עִוָּרוֺן noun [masculine] blindness ; — only in phrase (subject ׳י ), smite ( הִכָּה ) with blindness: figurative of 'blind incapacity' (Dr) ׳בְּע Deut 28:28 ; of smiting horses ׳בַּע Zech 12:4 , i.e. with blind staggers , making them helplessly wild. עַוֶּ֫רֶת noun feminine id.; — of sacrifice animals, abstract for concrete, Lev 22:22 (H).
